t: Section 7086(g) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking out “sections 751–756, 757–791, and 793” and inserting in place thereof “chapter 81”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical conforming amendment that replaces one cross-reference with another in title 10. No tempting reading really exists here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and involves no party outside the federal government in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “sections 751–756, 757–791, and 793” and inserting in place thereof “chapter 81”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to the United States Code, changing a cross-reference from specific section numbers to a chapter title. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative housekeeping provision.
qwen_block.s: Section 7086(g) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking out “sections 751–756, 757–791, and 793” and inserting in place thereof “chapter 81”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that changes a statutory cross-reference in 10 U.S.C. 7086(g). It does not mention any party outside the federal government taking part in a federal decision. Being a statutory amendment is not enough on its own, because the amendment creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking.** The only possible pull toward "Yes" is that the text amends a statute. But this amendment only swaps one cross-reference for another: it replaces a list of sections with "chapter 81", which is the federal workers' compensation chapter in title 5. Nothing here involves a public comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation with outsiders or a right to sue. So the answer is "No".
